prompt: Vertical 9:16 photograph on 35 mm colour negative film, taken at night in heavy London rain: a backlit advertising poster in the end panel of a glass bus shelter, shot square-on from the kerb at chest height and close enough that the poster's thin dark aluminium frame almost fills the whole picture, top to bottom. The poster is a glossy, slightly airbrushed election-style campaign photograph of the man from the reference image, head and shoulders in the upper half, holding a phone to his right ear with his right hand, looking straight into the lens with a broad, practised, reassuring smile and lifted brows, set against a flat deep magenta background. Across the lower third of the poster, in huge heavy condensed white sans-serif capitals, one line: "SAVE OUR NHS". The poster is in pin-sharp focus and perfectly flat; the even glow of the LED tubes behind it is the brightest light in the frame. Raindrops bead and run down the glass in front of it, and an ambulance's blue emergency light, just out of frame on the left, throws a hard cold-blue flash across the left side of the glass and the dark metal frame, with its headlights smeared as a faint reflection in the glass over the magenta background, never over the letters. A sodium-orange street lamp overhead gilds the top edge of the frame; teal shadows, fine film grain, wet tarmac glinting below. No other text anywhere: no party name, no logo, no small print, no web address, no readable signs or plates. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 photograph on 35 mm film at night, taken from inside the cab of a stopped ambulance, looking sideways out through its rain-spattered passenger window at a bus shelter on the pavement a few metres away. The dark edge of the window frame and the door's inner trim run down the left and bottom edges of the picture, lit in pulses of blue from the ambulance's own emergency lights bouncing off the wet bodywork, while raindrops and streaks cling to the outer corners of the glass. Through the clear middle of the window, filling well over half the frame's height and in sharp focus, is the shelter's backlit end-panel poster, glowing evenly from LED tubes behind it inside a thin dark metal frame: a glossy campaign portrait of the man from the reference image, head and shoulders, holding a phone to his right ear with his right hand, eyes to camera, a wide confident smile, on a flat deep magenta background, and beneath his face, in enormous heavy condensed white sans-serif capitals, the single line "SAVE OUR NHS". The shelter's glass side panes and perch bench sit dim and empty beside it; a sodium-orange street lamp behind the shelter hazes the rain into an orange glow, and the pavement in front reflects the poster's light in a long wet smear. Cold teal shadows, visible film grain, slight halation round the bright panel. The slogan is the only readable text in the frame: no party name, logo, small print, timetable writing, signs or number plates. Thanks.
